plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial producing large, fragrant, bowl-shaped to fully double blooms atop sturdy stems with deeply lobed green foliage. A beloved cottage garden staple that can live for decades.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to Siberia, Mongolia, and northern China; widely cultivated in temperate gardens of North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Peonies are often hosted by ants, which feed on the sugary nectar on the buds, but the ants are not required for the flowers to open. Some peony plants can live and bloom for more than 50 years.

plants.name: Rosa canina
plants.description: A vigorous, arching, thorny deciduous shrub of hedgerows and woodland edges with delicate, five-petaled, lightly scented flowers, followed by bright red rose hips in autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (late May to July)
plants.location: Hedgerows, scrub and woodland margins across Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia
plants.funFact: Rose hips from the dog rose are extremely rich in vitamin C and were made into syrup in Britain during World War II when citrus fruits were scarce.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A graceful, semi-deciduous tree with fern-like foliage that bursts into spectacular clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, carpeting the ground beneath when they drop.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (May to June); October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in subtropical regions including California, Mexico, Florida, the Mediterranean, and parts of Africa
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacaranda trees line the streets, earning it the nickname Jacaranda City, though these trees bloom there in October.

plants.name: Banksia serrata
plants.description: A rugged, gnarled Australian tree or shrub with serrated, leathery leaves and tall, cylindrical flower spikes made of thousands of tiny individual flowers, which later develop into woody seed cones.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to winter in Australia (roughly February to August), including early June
plants.location: Eastern coast of Australia, in coastal heath, dunes, and open woodland from Queensland to Victoria and Tasmania
plants.funFact: Banksia seed cones are adapted to fire, often holding seeds for years until a bushfire heats them to release the seeds, and the 'Banksia men' of May Gibbs' children's stories were based on these cones.
